user.title: Connect to a Sigur server
user.description: Enable the SKUD integration port in the Sigur server management tool and give the operator the "OIF protocol access (Integrations)" right. OIF 1.8 sends the password in clear text inside the protocol, so TLS is strongly recommended.

data_description.port: TCP port of the OIF integration listener, 3312 by default.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turning this off lets anyone on the path read the OIF password. Only do it on a trusted network.
data_description.ca_bundle: Needed when the Sigur server uses a private certificate authority.
data_description.client_certificate: Only needed when the Sigur server requires mutual TLS authentication.

reauth_confirm.title: Sigur credentials rejected
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the operator credentials for {name} again.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure the Sigur server
reconfigure.description: Change the address or the TLS settings. Existing devices and entities are kept.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the Sigur server. Check the address, the port, and that the SKUD integration port is enabled.
error.invalid_auth: The operator login or password was rejected.
error.oif_disabled: This operator does not have the "OIF protocol access (Integrations)" right.
error.permission_denied: The operator is not allowed to use this part of the protocol.
error.invalid_certificate: The TLS certificate could not be validated. Check the CA bundle and the client certificate.
error.unsupported_version: The Sigur server does not support the requested OIF version.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_configured: This Sigur server is already configured.

data.enable_personal_data: Expose personal data in entities and events
data.resolve_object_names: Resolve access object names on demand

data_description.scan_interval: How often GETAPINFO is polled. Events update entities immediately, so this is only a safety net.
data_description.enable_control: Off by default. Turning this on lets Home Assistant lock, unlock and open doors.
data_description.enable_personal_data: Off by default. Turning this on shows names and object ids in entities, events and diagnostics.
data_description.resolve_object_names: Fetches a name with GETOBJECTINFO when an event does not carry one. Results are cached briefly.

data.enable_backfill: Recover missed events after a reconnect
data.backfill_on_first_start: Also backfill on the very first start
data.debug_raw_events: Include the raw protocol message in events

data_description.enable_backfill: Uses GETHISTORY over a bounded window after a reconnect. Duplicates are removed.
data_description.backfill_on_first_start: Off by default, so a fresh install does not import old history into the recorder.
data_description.debug_raw_events: Diagnostic only. The raw message can contain personal data.

webhook.title: Outbound webhook
webhook.description: Optional and off by default. A standard Home Assistant automation with rest_command or MQTT is usually the better choice.

data.webhook_enabled: Forward events to an external endpoint
data.webhook_allow_insecure: Allow plain HTTP to a private address

data_description.webhook_secret: Each delivery is signed over its timestamp, nonce and body.
data_description.webhook_categories: Leave empty to forward everything that is published.
data_description.webhook_allow_insecure: Dangerous. Only for an endpoint on a private network.

error.webhook_url_required: An endpoint URL is required when the webhook is enabled.
error.webhook_https_required: The endpoint must use HTTPS, unless it is a private address and insecure delivery is confirmed.
error.webhook_secret_required: A signing secret is required when the webhook is enabled.

trigger_type.tamper: The enclosure of {entity_name} was tampered with

set_access_point_mode.name: Set access point mode
set_access_point_mode.description: Sets the lock mode of one or more Sigur access points. Requires control to be enabled in the integration options.

confirm_all_access_points.name: Confirm all access points
confirm_all_access_points.description: Extra confirmation required when the call targets every access point of a server.

allow_pass.name: Allow a pass
allow_pass.description: Authorises a single pass through an access point. Requires control to be enabled in the integration options.

object_id.name: Access object ID
object_id.description: Numeric ID of the employee, guest or car. Leave empty for an anonymous pass.

refresh.name: Refresh
refresh.description: Polls the targeted Sigur servers immediately.

set_access_point_camera.name: Attach a camera
set_access_point_camera.description: Records which camera belongs to an access point. The camera entity is what shows a picture; the RTSP URL is stored for automations and a future camera platform. Calling this with neither field clears the binding.

camera_entity_id.name: Camera entity
camera_entity_id.description: An existing camera entity. Its snapshot appears on the access point tile in the Sigur panel.

rtsp_url.name: RTSP URL
rtsp_url.description: Stored as-is. A browser cannot play RTSP directly, so this alone does not display video anywhere.

direction_mode.name: Pass direction
direction_mode.description: Which way people may pass. OIF does not report this, so it is declared here. A one-way access point only offers the button for that direction.

oif_access_disabled.title: Sigur: OIF access is disabled for this operator
oif_access_disabled.description: The operator configured for {name} does not have the "OIF protocol access (Integrations)" right. Grant it in the Sigur operator settings, then reload the integration.

invalid_certificate.title: Sigur: the TLS certificate could not be validated
invalid_certificate.description: The certificate presented by {name} was rejected. Check that it has not expired and that the configured CA bundle matches the Sigur certificate store.

unsupported_version.title: Sigur: unsupported OIF version
unsupported_version.description: The server {name} rejected the configured OIF version. Reconfigure the integration with a version this server supports.

server_unavailable.title: Sigur: the server has been unreachable
server_unavailable.description: Home Assistant has not been able to reach {name} for a while. Check the server, the network path and that the SKUD integration port is still enabled.

control_disabled.message: Control of the Sigur system {name} is disabled. Turn on "Allow controlling access points" in the integration options first.

set_mode_failed.message: Sigur refused to set the mode of access point {ap_id}: {error}

allow_pass_failed.message: Sigur refused a pass through access point {ap_id}: {error}
